title: Very + Adjective Killer
intro: Very tired becomes exhausted. Very scared becomes terrified. One strong word instead of two weak ones — straight out of the Cambridge writing mark scheme.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very hungry'
a stronger way to say 'very cold'
A2.why: “It's freezing!” Not literally ice, just very cold.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very hot'
A2.why: Like boiling water: Valencia in August.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very small'
A2.why: One word does the job of “very small”.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very big'
A2.why: Never “very huge”: huge already means very big.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very tired'
a stronger way to say 'very happy'
A2.why: “I'm delighted to meet you”: very happy and polite.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very angry'
A2.why: The sheriff was furious: very, very angry.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very wet'
A2.why: Wet right through, like after a summer storm.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very bad'
a stronger way to say 'very interesting'
A2.why: A fascinating museum keeps you there all day.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'very full' or 'very crowded'
A2.why: The metro during Fallas is packed.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very frightened'
a stronger way to say 'very dirty'
B1.why: Filthy boots after a day on the ranch.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very clean'
B1.why: Not a single spot: a spotless hospital ward.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very old'
B1.why: Ancient Rome, ancient walls: very, very old.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very new'
B1.why: Just out of the box, never used.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very beautiful'
B1.why: Enthusiastic and informal: a gorgeous sunset.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very ugly'
a stronger way to say 'very tiring'
B1.why: -ing describes the thing (an exhausting day); -ed describes you.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very funny'
B1.why: So funny you can't stop laughing.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very loud'
B1.why: So loud you can't hear: the mascletà is deafening.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very valuable'
B1.why: Spanish trap: priceless means worth a fortune, not “sin precio” or worthless.

B1.right: a stronger way to say 'very thirsty'
B1.why: Dry like the desert after a long ride.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very frightened' — frozen with fear
B2.why: Like a stone (“petra”): too scared to move.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very angry'
B2.why: So angry your face changes colour.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very happy'
B2.why: Wildly happy, like Valencia fans after a win.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very upset'
an even stronger way to say 'very clean or tidy'
B2.why: Perfectly clean, without a single mark.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very big'
B2.why: From the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant statue.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very small'
an even stronger way to say 'very hungry'
an even stronger way to say 'very surprised'
B2.why: So surprised you can hardly believe it.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very hot' — about the weather or sun
B2.why: A scorching day in the desert, or in Seville in July.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very wet'
B2.why: Completely wet, as if someone threw a bucket at you.

B2.right: an even stronger way to say 'very interesting'
B2.why: So gripping you can't put the book down.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very angry' — formal register
C1.why: Common in formal writing: “an irate customer”.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very happy' — a moment of triumph
C1.why: Lifted up by success: elated after passing the exam.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very poor' — with nothing left
C1.why: No home, no food, no money at all.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very mean with money' — formal
C1.why: Formal and critical: someone who hates spending even a cent.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very upset' — cannot be comforted
C1.why: Nothing anyone says can make them feel better.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very expensive'
the strongest way to say 'very small' — used for an amount
C1.why: British spelling -re: a meagre salary, a meagre meal.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very important or large in scale'
C1.why: Like a monument: a monumental mistake or achievement.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very painful'
the strongest way to say 'very old and falling apart' — about a building
C1.why: Broken windows, falling roof: a dilapidated farmhouse.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very hungry for more' — never satisfied
C1.why: Can't be satisfied: an insatiable appetite for gold.

C1.right: the strongest way to say 'very difficult' — long and tiring
C1.why: An arduous journey west by wagon.
